sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Publishing of PC and Console Video Games via Digital Stores

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Continental Law; unitary national jurisdiction)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Double Taxation Agreements concluded by Luxembourg covering over 85 jurisdictions, including France, Germany, Belgium, Netherlands, China, Singapore, UAE, and the United States
Bilateral Investment Treaties concluded under the Belgo-Luxembourg Economic Union framework
EU Free Trade Agreements applicable to Luxembourg, including EU-Japan, EU-Korea, EU-Singapore, EU-Vietnam, EU-Canada CETA, and EU-Mercosur in its approved form

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies, as amended, Book II provisions governing limited partnerships including the special limited partnership, supplemented by the Law of 12 July 2016 introducing the SCSp; Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended; Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE), as amended; Grand-Ducal Regulation of 1 March 2019 on the RBE; CSSF Regulation 12-02 on AML/CFT, as amended; Luxembourg Criminal Code Articles 506-1 et seq.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport of each ultimate beneficial owner, general partner, limited partner, and authorized signatory
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport issuing authority or competent consular authority in the country of nationality
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; consular legalization if the issuing state is not a party to the Apostille Convention

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address (utility bill, bank statement, or equivalent) for each UBO and controller
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider, regulated bank, or public authority in the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization, depending on the issuing jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing or official registry excerpt of each corporate UBO or corporate general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent companies registry in the entity's country of incorporation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarially certified power of attorney for the Luxembourg formation agent and registered office service provider
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the jurisdiction of execution

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Ultimate beneficial owner declaration and notarized signature specimen
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or competent licensing authority in the country of origin

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based customer due diligence must be completed before the SCSp is filed. The formation file must contain positive identification of all direct and indirect beneficial owners holding at least 25% of interests, control through other means, or control of a corporate general partner. Screening is mandatory against the CSSF AML/CFT framework, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list, OFAC SDN list, Luxembourg national financial sanctions, and internal politically exposed person databases. PEPs, their family members, and close associates must receive enhanced due diligence. Any inability to identify a beneficial owner must be documented and will delay incorporation.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés online platform (lbr.lu / rcs.lu)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Statutory filing language is French, with Luxembourgish, French, and German recognized as administrative languages. The SCSp name must include 'Société en Commandite Spéciale' or the abbreviation 'SCSp' before or after the chosen name. Names in non-Latin script must be submitted in a romanized transliteration. Foreign-language names are accepted if intelligible and not contrary to Luxembourg public order, but the legal form indicator must appear in the official registered name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name reservation is valid for 30 days and is not automatically extendable. A new reservation may be filed after expiry. If the RCS rejects a proposed name, the applicant may file a request for reconsideration with the Luxembourg Business Registers within one month of the written rejection. If reconsideration is denied, an administrative appeal may be brought before the Tribunal administratif through a Luxembourg-licensed lawyer within three months of notification. An alternative reserved name may be submitted at any point before or during the appeal process.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For an SCSp, a physical registered office address in Luxembourg is mandatory. A pure virtual office or mailbox-only address is not acceptable for registration. A commercial domiciliation service may provide a physical registered office address, but it must be a real location capable of receiving official notices and legal correspondence. The digital game publishing business model must also maintain records in Luxembourg if it seeks to evidence commercial substance.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate. For a compliant, non-regulated low-risk software publishing entity with a genuine registered office, the estimated annual likelihood of unannounced physical inspection is below 10%. If the registered office is a bare virtual office, nominee management is used, or UBO/RBE filings are incomplete, the risk rises to 30-35%.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Loi modifiée du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales (Commercial Companies Law), as amended by the Law of 23 July 2016; Articles 101-108 (Société en Commandite Spéciale, SCSp)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Acte constitutif / Contrat de société (Constitutive Deed and Partnership Agreement) filed electronically via LBR e-Filing
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital for an SCSp; no mandatory escrow account. Contributions are agreed contractually in the partnership agreement and may be in cash or in kind, subject to valuation rules and creditor protection only for in-kind contributions.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED FIRST: The subscription and acceptance of partnership interests in the SCSp, as set forth in the consolidated annexes, is hereby approved, and the General Partner is authorized to sign the constitutive act and open a bank collection account. SECOND: The registered office is hereby adopted at 412F, Route d’Esch, L-2086 Luxembourg, and the filing of official forms with the Luxembourg Business Registers is ratified. THIRD: Ms. Paulina Kantor is appointed as Sole Manager of the General Partner, and Ms. Claire Hoffmann as Compliance Officer, each to serve until replaced, with authority to execute filings, authorise signature mandates, and complete all establishment formalities before the RCS, tax authority, and postal employers’ registration for personnel benefits.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of Constitutive Act / Partnership Agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public of Luxembourg (for optional notarial deed) or direct signature by all partners with date-stamping; the RCS accepts either route unless real estate is contributed.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the partnership agreement in Luxembourgish, English, or French. Include name, registered office, corporate object, partner identities, capital contribution schedule, management provisions, profit sharing, and termination rules. Each partner or an authorised duly appointed attorney-in-fact must sign. If a notarial deed is used, submit original copy to the notary for certification; otherwise retain the deed in private custody for later RCS filing.
required_dossiers: Draft partnership agreement / acte constitutif
Valid passport or national ID of each partner
Extract from criminal record (less than 3 months) for each general partner
Consent letter for registered office use
Power of attorney if acting through a representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or a partner identifies a legal defect (e.g., invalid object, lack of authority), amend the agreement and re-execute; no monetary penalty if corrected before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – RCS (lbr.lu, e-Filing portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log on to LBR e-Filing, download Form C (entity creation), upload the signed partnership agreement, provide details of partners and managers, confirm the registered office, and submit. Pay the registration fee online. The RCS assigns a permanent registration number upon validation. Registration must occur within one month after execution of the constitutive act.
required_dossiers: Form C duly completed
Certified copy of the signed partnership agreement
Municipal registered-office consent letter with dated copy of the lease
Identity documents and criminal record extracts for the managers/general partners
Power of attorney if filed by agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a query (defect in forms, missing translation, or residence issue), submit a corrective e-fair within 15 days. Use the RCS 'amend' service to correct clerical mistakes; formal appeals may go to the district court if refused.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in the Electronic Official Gazette (RESA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations (RESA) – administered by Luxembourg Business Registers / Ministry of Justice
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After RCS registration, the registry coordinates automatic publication of a legal notice in RESA. The notice must contain the SCSp name, legal form, registered office, partners' liability information, and registration number. No separate action is generally required; however, verify online that the RESA extract appears within 2 business days.
required_dossiers: RCS registration certificate
Copy of the partnership agreement
Extract of the entry in the RCS ledger
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If RESA publication is delayed, contact the RCS public service desk to request re-sending of the transmission; if publication is incomplete, apply to the RCS for a corrective supplementary notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, VAT and Direct Tax Notification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD); Administration de l'Enregistrement, des Domaines et de la TVA (AEDT)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the standard business tax registration form (Formulaire P) with the ACD to obtain a Luxembourg corporate tax reference number. Submit the VAT registration request under the standard Luxembourg VAT law if the entity will perform taxable digital publishing services. Use the portal 'MyGuichet.lu' or a tax agent. The SCSp is fiscally transparent; the notification establishes the tax file for each partner.
required_dossiers: RCS registration certificate
Partnership agreement
List of managing and general partners with residence addresses
Pro-forma invoice or description of intended digital publishing activities
Authorisation of a local tax agent, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax authority requests additional information on taxable nexus, respond within 30 days with a statement of place of establishment and the electronic service place-of-supply analysis under Article 57 of the VAT Law; alternatively, obtain a precognition ruling from the ACD.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Occupational Safety, Municipal Occupancy and Optional Licences
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Labour – Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM); Ville de Luxembourg – Municipal Office; Corps Grand-Ducal d'Incendie et de Secours (CGDIS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: For an office-only activity, secure a municipal certificate of occupancy or a simple change-of-use declaration if the leased space is classified as office. Submit a workplace conformity declaration to ITM when hiring employees. Arrange a fire-safety audit by a licensed inspector; in buildings with public access, obtain a fire department conformity certificate. Register with the Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS) for employee social security. No industrial licence is required for Steam/console publishing.
required_dossiers: Lease agreement for the registered office
Municipal occupancy certificate request
Workplace health and safety declaration (ITM form)
Fire-safety audit report / certificate of conformity
Employee registration forms with CCSS (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If ITM issues a non-compliance order, remedy the identified deficiencies within the indicated deadline (e.g., correct ergonomics, install emergency exits or required signage), then ask for a re-inspection. If the municipal certificate is refused, provide proof of zoning compatibility of the address; if CGDS requires extinguishers, upload the purchase certificate and request modification of the report.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de l'Économie – Department of Industry and Digital Services (for consultation only; no application required)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No specific statutory licence for digital game publishing under Luxembourg law. An RCS registration and a VAT number are sufficient for lawful operation. The activity falls outside the scope of the Law of 10 June 1999 on classified establishments.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: EXEMPT – Software publishing does not constitute a classified installation under Annex 1 of the 10 June 1999 law; therefore a full EIA report is not required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater or VOCs are generated. If the premises house a computer server room or accumulated electronic equipment, disposal must comply with the EU WEEE Directive (2012/19/EU) and the Luxembourg law of 16 July 2019 on electronic waste. General office waste must be separated and collected by an authorised municipal contractor.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Office occupation requires a municipal occupancy or building conformity declaration. Fire-safety compliance is limited to correct egress, alarms and extinguishers as verified by a CGDIS-approved inspector. No structural load clearance is required because the activity is office-based. If employees are engaged, register with the ITM for occupational health and with the CCSS for employment coverage.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct taxes; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT; official portal: guichet.lu
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities must first register with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS) via the guichet.lu one-stop-shop to obtain a business registration number, then obtain a Luxembourg tax number and VAT number from the AEDT. Non-resident entities without a fixed establishment must register for VAT directly with the AEDT using the applicable registration form before commencing taxable supplies in Luxembourg.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: The SCSp is mandatorily tax-transparent for Luxembourg income tax and has no separate legal personality; no check-the-box election exists. Partners may elect to join a Luxembourg VAT group (assujetti unique) under Article 68 of the VAT Law if the statutory conditions are met, and advance tax rulings may be obtained from the ACD for classification confirmation. Anti-hybrid rules under ATAD may override or recharacterise transparent structures where a mismatched outcome arises.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 30,000 annual taxable turnover for the small-business franchise; otherwise no threshold applies and registration is mandatory from the first euro of taxable supplies, including for non-resident suppliers making taxable distance sales of digital services.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance mandate exists for B2B/B2C transactions; e-invoicing is permitted. Mandatory e-invoicing applies only to B2G invoices under the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 28 January 2019 via the PEPPOL network. VAT returns and EC Sales Lists must be filed electronically through the AEDT portal.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Article 43 of the Luxembourg VAT Law, supplies of goods dispatched or transported outside the EU are zero-rated subject to documentary evidence of export. Digital services supplied via Steam or PlayStation Store are not zero-rated; the place of supply is determined under Articles 58 and 59 of the VAT Law (B2C and B2B), meaning Luxembourg VAT is chargeable only where the customer is established, resident, or habitually located in Luxembourg. Supplies to non-EU B2B customers fall outside Luxembourg VAT and are reportable under the reverse-charge mechanism in the customer's jurisdiction.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Déclaration d'exportation) – mandatory for physical export of goods
Bill of Lading, CMR, or Airway Bill – mandatory transport evidence for physical export of goods
Inward Remittance Certificate or equivalent payment proof – required for export validation and FX repatriation where applicable
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Under Articles 80 and 81 of the Luxembourg VAT Law, erroneous zero-rating triggers immediate VAT reassessment, interest at 0.6% per month, and administrative fines ranging from EUR 750 to EUR 12,500 plus a corrective assessment up to 20% of the tax due. Fraudulent claims constitute a criminal offence under Article 88 of the VAT Law with penalties including imprisonment and fines up to double the evaded tax. The AEDT may claw back zero-rated supplies retroactively for up to 5 years, extended to 10 years in cases of fraud.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), acting within the Eurosystem and in coordination with the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) for AML/CFT and forex counterparty supervision. Luxembourg maintains a full liberalized foreign exchange regime under EU law; no separate Luxembourg foreign exchange administration approval is required for current or capital transactions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible in Luxembourg for both current and capital account transactions. Profit remittance, dividends, partnership distributions, and liquidation proceeds can be paid abroad without prior authorisation or repatriation taxes. The only constraints are standard EU/AML reporting, tax withholding on certain payments (e.g., withholding tax on dividends under domestic law, subject to treaties and EU Directives), and balance-of-payments statistical reporting to the BCL for transactions above €12,500. For an SCSp with pass-through tax status, distributions to non-resident partners are generally not subject to Luxembourg withholding tax because the SCSp is considered fiscally transparent, provided no Luxembourg commercial substance creates an unexpected taxable nexus.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Luxembourg imposes no export proceeds surrender requirement, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no statutory repatriation deadline. Export receipts, including digital store proceeds from Steam and PlayStation, may be held in the original currency (USD/EUR) or converted at freely agreed market rates. The SCSp must only ensure that transactions are booked consistently for tax and balance-of-payments purposes; BCL statistical declarations apply when individual EUR/USD equivalent transactions exceed €12,500.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE / Spuerkeess)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: LOW to MEDIUM for the primary treasury function. Under PSD2, an Electronic Money Institution (EMI) such as Wise, Revolut Business, or Airwallex is not a full credit institution and cannot provide depository-guaranteed escrow or commercial-lending services. EMIs are viable for low-value inbound royalty collections after initial bank onboarding, especially USD montant receipt from platforms, but they are not acceptable for the statutory capital-level or partner capital projections in an SCSp. Legal constraints include: EMI accounts are not 'bank accounts' in the strict legal sense; no deposit guarantee protection under Luxembourg legal deposit guarantee scheme; EMI providers may not support an SCSp partnership structure with non-resident partners due to their simplified KYC and may freeze funds if the ultimate beneficial ownership chain is opaque. An SCSp should use EMIs only as a sub-account payment rail for developer payouts, never as the primary controlled treasury cash pool.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Under CSSF AML/CFT regulations, remote digital onboarding is permitted when a bank uses a CSSF-certified video identification solution or an approved eIDAS electronic identification scheme. In practice, however, mandatory physical presence is not a statutory rule, but most tier-1 Luxembourg banks require at least one manual/video interview with the SCSp's general partner (Gérant), the effective manager, and a natural-person UBO. Where the SCSp is managed by an unregulated corporate general partner, the bank will require identification of the individuals controlling that GP. Remote opening is possible for low-risk operational accounts if the GP and all UBOs are EU/EEA residents and hold certified passports; for capital escrow accounts or accounts receiving large Steam/PlayStation payouts, a wet-ink signature and notarized/official certification of the partnership agreement are usually mandated.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Pass-through partnership classification with no local employees, no physical registered office, and uncertain substance triggers bank classification as a 'high-risk legal vehicle'
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a full notarized/registered SCSp partnership agreement, the CSSF/Mexico trade register excerpt (RCS), current certificate of domiciliation, proof of registered office, annual financial projections, substance description (real managerial activity, general partner management), and a written explanation of the commercial rationale for the SCSp as the publisher-of-record under the Steam/PlayStation contracts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) resides in a high-risk third country or is not identified due to chain of foreign corporate partners
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit a copied-up UBO register under the Luxembourg Registry of Beneficial Owners (RBE), passports and proof of residential address for every natural-person UBO with >25% economic interest, clear source-of-wealth documentation (asset origin, prior corporate salary, capital gain tax returns), and a corroborated business history of the UBO's role in the global venture.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Receipts from digital gaming platforms (Steam/PlayStation) flagged as high transaction velocity, cross-border dispersed counterparties, or prepaid-card-like settlement flow
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Supply executed commercial agreements with Valve Corp and PlayStation (Sony Interactive Entertainment), a reconciliation of forecasted store payout reports, a written treasury flowchart showing gross receipt to developer-royalty distribution, and a compliance memo confirming game classification as non-Qat and non-gambling content. Should also include VAT/GST analysis regarding digital gaming revenue if the SCSp performs EU merchant-of-record duties.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital injections combined with immediate onward payment to foreign development studios without a clear corresponding service or ownership: 'round-tripping' risk
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Maintain a capital contribution ledger with bank-stamped MT103 and notice of credit (NOC), the capital call calendar and partners' written capital commitment letters, each developer agreement with milestones and IP acceptance certificates, and board/GP resolutions authorizing each disbursement. Include invoices from development studios and proof of digital asset deliverables (steam store build IDs, console certification reports) to demonstrate the real economic quid pro quo.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All capital contributions from the SCSp's limited partners or parent entity should be routed via SWIFT MT103 (or MT202 for substantial European interbank-only transfers if the ultimate beneficiary account is held in the same EU bank) to the designated Luxembourg IBAN. The payment must refer to 'SCSp Capital Contribution - [Partner name] - Capital Call dated [date]'. EU harmonized purpose codes 'INVE' (investment) or 'EQUI' (equity-like capital injection) are recommended; for subordinated shareholder loans, use 'MOLA' (working capital/monetary asset) or 'LOAN' with a written subordination deed. The bank will require source-of-funds evidence for the remitter, the attested capital call letter, and if the injection is non-cash (e.g., IP assignment), specialized valuation and notarized transfer protocols. No BCL approval is needed, but aggregate transfers above €12,500 trigger balance-of-payments reporting.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For developer royalty and license payouts from the SCSp treasury account, the recommended clearing rail is SWIFT MT103 with purpose code 'ROYA' (royalties) or 'LICF' (license fees), including the contract reference and net-of-VAT amount. For physical merchandise or console asset procurement (e.g., development kits, promotional merchandise), the SCSp may use a commercial letter of credit (documentary credit) through a Luxembourg confirming bank; however, digital-first PC/console publishing is primarily B2B service-based and does not require LC. For bulk recurring Steam/PlayStation platform payout reconciliations, the SCSp will maintain an aggregated EUR/USD liquidity reserve in a single concentration account. Standard ACH/Sepà is acceptable for EU/EEA developer payouts; non-EEA payouts must use MT103 with Beneficiary Legal Name matching the tax/VAT documentation to avoid sanctions filtering.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/USD Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) for offshore USD clearing, if bank cannot liquid-settle in certain geographies
EUR/USD Cross-Currency Swaps (interest rate and principal exchange)
Currency Options (plain vanilla calls/puts) when required for a hedge in lieu of nudging the pass-through tax profile

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts (comptes annuels) filed by the general partner on behalf of the SCSp
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months of financial-year end; for a 31 December year-end, approval by 30 June and RCS deposit by 31 July
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing exposes the general partner to fines from €500 to €25,000; persistent failure for two consecutive years may trigger RCS administrative strike-off (radiation d'office) proceedings

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial ownership data (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs – RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: RBE maintained by Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: At least once per calendar year, within 1 month of the anniversary of the SCSp's RBE registration date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative late fines of €250–€1,250; wilful omission or false declaration triggers criminal sanctions of 8 days–6 months' imprisonment and/or fines of €750–€25,000 for responsible officers

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual approval of financial statements by partners (internal governance milestone)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Not filed; recorded in the partnership minute book and signed by the general partner
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months of financial-year end (mandatory precondition to the RCS filing deadline)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No direct government penalty; failure to approve on time delays the RCS annual-accounts filing and thereby attracts the late-filing and strike-off sanctions of the first matrix row

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit (réviseur d'entreprises agréé) where the SCSp exceeds any two of: balance-sheet total above €4.4 million, net turnover above €8.8 million, or average workforce above 50 employees; audit is also mandatory if the partnership agreement or a partner requires it
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP under the Law of 19 December 2002 on the RCS and annual accounts; IFRS as endorsed by the EU is permitted as an alternative reporting framework

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The general partner must re-attest the SCSp's RBE file annually within one month of the registration anniversary, restating each natural-person beneficial owner (direct or indirect interest exceeding 25%, senior managing official fallback), and must update the register within 30 days of any share-transfer or ownership change
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (partners) of the SCSp, kept by the general partner
Register of Directors/Managers of the corporate general partner
Minute Book of partner resolutions and general-partner management decisions
Ownership ledger corroborating the RBE declaration

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: $3,000 – $7,500 per annum for domiciliation and corporate-secretarial retainer charged by a Luxembourg PFS or fiduciary
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $3,500 – $8,500 for a full statutory audit when triggered; most SCSp structures remain below the audit thresholds and incur no audit fee

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% aggregate Luxembourg City rate (17% corporate income tax + 1.19% unemployment solidarity surcharge + 6.75% municipal business tax); SCSp is fiscally transparent, so this rate applies to resident corporate partners on their allocable profit share, while resident individual partners are taxed at progressive personal income tax rates.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 80% exemption on qualifying IP income (IP box); 100% participation exemption on qualifying dividends and capital gains for resident corporate partners (10% holding or EUR 1.2 million acquisition cost); notional interest deduction on new equity; investment tax credit; double deduction for foreign shareholding losses; 0% WHT on outbound royalties and interest.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulaire 720 (Déclaration pour l'impôt sur le revenu des collectivités) filed via the Luxembourg direct tax e-filing platform (myguichet.lu / eCDF) using LuxTrust business authentication.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 31 May of the calendar year following the fiscal year-end; automatic extension to 31 December where the return is filed electronically by an approved Luxembourg tax adviser.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, RCS registration number, LEI, registered office in Luxembourg, and competent tax office (bureau d'imposition).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State the Luxembourg establishment address of the SCSp even when all partners are non-residents; a Luxembourg tax representative may be required.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Opening and closing dates of the accounting year; the SCSp may use a calendar year or an adopted business year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Align the filing period with Steam/PlayStation payout statements to ensure reconciliation of reported revenue.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Financial statements in EUR, disclosing game publishing revenue, platform commissions, co-publishing costs, and other operating results of the Luxembourg permanent establishment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Convert foreign currency disbursements at the official ACD exchange rate; report all Luxembourg-source sales generated through the SCSp's PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation of commercial profit to taxable profit; claims for the 80% IP-box exemption, participation exemption, notional interest deduction, and 17-year tax-loss carryforwards.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners are not taxable in Luxembourg unless the SCSp is deemed to carry on a Luxembourg PE or derives income from Luxembourg real estate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocation schedule of net profit or loss to each partner according to the partnership agreement, including each partner's tax residence, profit share, and allocated amount.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach a tax residence certificate for each non-resident partner claiming treaty relief; report the beneficial owner identifiers (RBE consistency).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a demand letter and an automatic surcharge of 10% of the assessed tax; late-payment interest accrues at 0.6% per month; failure to file the SCSp transparency return is administratively fined EUR 250 to EUR 5,000 per offence, and the ACD may assess the allocation ex officio.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulaire 710 (Déclaration pour l'impôt commercial communal) filed with the Administration des contributions directes on behalf of the commune (Luxembourg City rate 6.75%).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Same annual cycle as Formulaire 720: 31 May, extended to 31 December for e-filing by an approved Luxembourg tax adviser.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable business profit adjusted under the municipal business tax code and the taxable capital base of the enterprise.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The SCSp is liable to municipal business tax as an enterprise carrying on business in Luxembourg even when fully foreign-owned; maintain payroll and marketing evidence of PE substance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocation percentages for multi-commune activity, if any.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A single Luxembourg City establishment should be declared unless further permanent establishments exist.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Municipal investment tax credit and other statutory deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only where qualifying Luxembourg investment assets exist.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Same late-filing surcharge regime applicable to the corporate income tax return: 10% surcharge on the municipal business tax due, 0.6% monthly interest, ex officio assessment, and enforcement of arrears against the general partner.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% statutory rate on dividends paid by Luxembourg collective entities; distributions by the SCSp are transparent profit withdrawals and carry 0% Luxembourg withholding tax; the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive reduces the 15% to 0% where a corporate partner holds at least 10% for 12 months.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: A partner invoking a double tax treaty must hold the beneficial ownership of the income and submit a certificate of tax residence issued by its home tax authority; the Luxembourg withholding agent applies the reduced rate at source upon validated notification (Form 22), or the excess is reclaimed through the ACD refund procedure within five years; for SCSp structures, treaty access for non-resident partners follows the OECD partnership report, requiring the partner to be the beneficial owner of the allocated income.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Luxembourg imposes no statutory withholding tax on outbound royalties (0%) and no statutory withholding tax on outbound interest (0%); treaty rates are typically 0% under most DTAs; Steam/PlayStation platform licence fees paid to Valve Corp. or Sony are therefore paid gross from Luxembourg.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File mandatory where aggregate non-financial intercompany transactions exceed EUR 500,000 or financial intercompany transactions exceed EUR 250,000; Master File mandatory where worldwide group consolidated revenue equals or exceeds EUR 750 million; de minimis exemption applies to small enterprises (balance sheet below EUR 4.4 million and turnover below EUR 8.8 million).
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg does not apply UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations; substance is enforced through LIR Article 6 GAAR, ATAD anti-abuse rules, the OECD principal-purpose test, beneficial ownership requirements, and administrative practice requiring the SCSp to hold real local substance (registered office, local bookkeeping, management meetings in Luxembourg, local banking, and genuine decision-making) to obtain a tax residence certificate and treaty protection; the SCSp general partner must demonstrate central management and control in Luxembourg to avoid re-characterisation as an artificial arrangement.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly omitting Steam/PlayStation Store disbursements, fabricating platform commission deductions, destroying payout records, or submitting false declarations of the SCSp's allocable taxable profit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal fraude fiscale prosecution before Luxembourg courts: fines up to EUR 250,000 and imprisonment up to five years; ex officio tax assessment with 10% tax increase, monthly late interest of 0.6%, forfeiture of carry-forwards and incentives, and an extended 10-year statute of limitations for fraudulent suppression.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Members of the general partner management are jointly liable if they directed or supervised the fraud; courts may pierce the SCSp veil, order civil restitution of evaded tax, impose travel bans and asset freezes, and impose custodial sentences; the general partner bears unlimited personal liability for SCSp debts.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Manipulation and Hidden Profit Distribution
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging non-arm's-length commissions to the platform co-publisher, paying excessive royalties to a related IP-holding company, or shifting Steam sales profits to a zero-tax affiliate without functional, asset, and risk alignment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ACD reallocation under LIR Article 56 and the OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines; recharacterised excess is taxed as a hidden profit distribution subject to 15% withholding tax at source; interest accrues at 0.6% per month with a 10% surcharge, creating material double tax exposure; advance pricing agreement protection is revoked for misleading facts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign knowingly false transfer-pricing documentation face criminal complicity exposure and civil liability for resulting tax arrears; the general partner's unlimited liability extends to transfer-pricing restatements and unpaid withholding taxes.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Artificial Arrangement and Substance Deficiency (GAAR / Treaty Abuse)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a letterbox SCSp with no employees, no Luxembourg decision-making, no local bank account, and routing intellectual property royalties solely to access Luxembourg treaty exemptions or the 0% withholding tax regime without actual commercial activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of the Luxembourg tax residence certificate, denial of treaty benefits under the OECD principal-purpose test, recharacterisation under LIR Article 6, look-through taxation of foreign partners in Luxembourg and abroad, penalties up to 10% of tax due, and mandatory unwinding of the abusive structure.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managerial officers face professional disqualification and civil suits by co-partners and creditors; in flagrant cases, fiscal fraud charges trigger personal monetary liability, travel bans (interdiction de sortie du territoire), asset seizures, and imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to file or update the Luxembourg RBE (Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs) within one month, concealing the ultimate beneficial owner behind the SCSp's limited-partner silence, or executing Steam payouts without a documented KYC/AML vendor review (Low-Risk tier still requires written policies).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines from EUR 1,250 to EUR 25,000 for RBE breaches; criminal AML penalties under the law of 12 November 2004, as amended, including fines up to EUR 5 million and imprisonment up to five years for intentional violations; RBE registers are public and exchanged within the EU beneficial-ownership network.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the general partner and natural-person general partners are personally liable for AML failures; Luxembourg courts may impose director disqualification, personal fines, asset seizure, and custodial sanctions, and may authorise civil veil-piercing to satisfy tax and AML penalties.
